steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The human body has over 600 skeletal muscles . For GCSE PE, you must know the location and function of the major muscles listed below.

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: Muscles work in antagonistic pairs - when one muscle contracts (shortens), the other relaxes (lengthens). This allows bones to move at joints in opposite directions.

steps.title: Agonist (Prime Mover)
steps.body: The muscle that contracts to produce the desired movement. It is the main muscle responsible for the action.

steps.title: Antagonist
steps.body: The muscle that relaxes (lengthens) to allow the agonist to work. It may offer some controlled resistance to smooth the movement.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Name the antagonistic pair at the elbow joint and identify the agonist during flexion. | Explain the difference between concentric and eccentric isotonic contraction, giving a sporting example of each. | What is the role of a fixator muscle? Give an example from a sporting action.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: The antagonistic pair at the elbow is the biceps and triceps. The agonist during flexion is the biceps (it contracts to flex the elbow while the triceps relaxes). | Concentric: the muscle shortens while contracting - e.g. the quadriceps shortening during the upward phase of a squat. Eccentric: the muscle lengthens while contracting - e.g. the quadriceps lengtheni | A fixator stabilises the origin of the agonist muscle so it can work effectively. During a bicep curl, the deltoids contract isometrically to hold the shoulder still while the biceps works on the elbo

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always name the joint, the movement, and the specific muscle in your answers Use the words "contracts" and "relaxes" precisely - do not say a muscle "works" When asked about antagonistic pairs, name both muscles and state which contracts Concentric = shortening, Eccentric = lengthening under tension, Isometric = no change The agonist is also called the prime mover Isometric contractions are common in gymnastics holds, rugby scrums and yoga Muscle fibre types are Higher-tier content - make sure you can compare all three types
